statement: There are 15 children on a bus. 9 of them are girls and the rest are boys. How many boys are on the bus?

choices.misconception: I counted on from 9 to 15 and counted the 9 as well, so I got one too many.
I gave the number of girls instead of the number of boys.
I gave the number of all the children on the bus.
I added 15 and 9, but the girls are already part of the 15.

hints: The girls and the boys together make the whole bus.
Draw one long bar for all the children and split it into a girls part and a boys part. When you know the whole and one part, the other part is what is left over.
The whole is 15 and the girls part is 9. Count on from 9 up to 15, counting only the steps you take.

solutions.reliable: All 15 children are girls or boys. The girls are 9 of them, so the boys are 15 take away 9, which is 6. Check: 9 + 6 = 15. The idea to keep: whole minus one part gives the other part.

whyOnTest: Part and whole: the question gives the whole and one part, and adding the two numbers is the most common wrong move.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
